title: A member's agent meets {{castBrand}}'s MCP door
lede: How a {{castProgram}} member's own AI agent reaches {{castBrand}}: discover, register, consent, per-call token exchange, gateway, policy decision, human approval, audit. The agent is never trusted; every hop past discovery is inside {{castBrand}}'s boundary.

nodes.label: Audit + SIEM
sub: the agent has no write path

edges.label: {{castBrand}} publishes its MCP door to the catalog: URL, auth metadata, branding and privacy policy
Reviews it and lists it, so any member of the assistant can find it
Browses the catalog and adds the connector: free, nothing to install, no account to create
The connector appears in the member's own agent, not signed in yet
Calls the MCP tool with no token → 401 + resource_metadata
RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata: the authorization server is PingOne
Self-registers with a CIMD client document (or DCR, RFC 7591) and gets its own client identity
Opens the member's browser to PingOne (authorization code + PKCE)
Passkey or MFA, then consents on a screen that names this agent: read miles, redeem with approval
Authorization code; the agent redeems it with private_key_jwt client authentication
RFC 8693 exchange for one tool call (private_key_jwt)
Token: sub = member, act.client_id = agent, aud = one tool, minutes-long lifetime
Tool call with the bearer token (no DPoP on PingOne)
Validates aud and scope against the allowlist, then asks for a verdict on member, agent, tool and amount
Permit, deny or step-up; redeeming miles is spending, so approval is required
Pending approval that names the exact redemption (timeout is denial)
Reviews and approves in the {{castBrand}} app, never in the agent chat
Single-use approval receipt, spendable only for this transaction
Only allowed calls get through; reads ride the delegated token, the redemption carries the approval
Result returns through the gateway
Writes sub, act.client_id, jti, tool and verdict
Authorization server writes the same fields for every exchange

steps.title: Publish once, get it free
steps.what: {{castBrand}} lists its connector in the assistant's catalog once. After that a member adds it from the catalog for free: nothing to install, no account to create. Sign-in and consent come on first use.

steps.title: Discover
steps.what: The agent knocks with no token and gets a 401 that points at the metadata. The door advertises itself; nobody at {{castBrand}} is involved.

steps.title: Register
steps.what: The agent registers itself with a client document. Now {{castBrand}} has an identity to name in consent, scope, and switch off.

steps.title: Consent
steps.what: The member signs in at PingOne with a passkey. The consent screen names this agent and what it may do. The member session never enters the agent.

steps.title: Exchange, per call
steps.what: Every tool call gets its own token: subject is the member, actor is the agent, one audience, minutes to live. The agent holds nothing standing.

steps.title: Call + decide
steps.what: The call reaches only the gateway. It checks audience and scope, then asks Authorize for a verdict. Redeeming miles is spending, so the answer is approval required.

steps.title: Approve
steps.what: The approval happens in {{castBrand}}'s own app, naming the exact redemption. One approval, one action, and a timeout means no.

steps.title: Permit
steps.what: Only permitted calls reach the rewards service, which accepts only its own audience. The credentials for the legacy system never leave the Facade.

steps.title: Log and revoke
steps.what: Gateway and authorization server write the same record, in storage the agent cannot touch. Turn off the agent client and its access ends within one token lifetime.
